metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: data available from the corresponding author upon request
metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for simulation calibration and evaluation.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper states data is available from the corresponding author upon request in the Data Availability section.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle coordinates (xi, yi) from raw video frames to create position matrices mt. Matrices are down-sampled to 4x512 pixels and stacked across N=3 consecutive time steps to represent state st.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all parameters stated, but specific extraction tool for vehicle coordinates from raw video is not named.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Trains a CNN-based Q-network using Adam optimizer, experience replay, and a target network. Implements multitask learning to predict Q-values, mean speed, and queue length simultaneously.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all parameters and hardware stated; generic DRL framework used.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained DRL model against No-control and PI-ALINEA baselines in a SUMO simulation of a real-world freeway segment (Qingdao-Huangdao tunnel).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulator and key parameters named; specific SUMO version missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into 8 subareas and removes information from specific subareas to test the DRL controller's sensitivity to spatial data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, subarea division logic described but exact coordinates for subareas 1-8 are visual only.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves for episode reward and mean travel time during the DRL training phase.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training parameters and simulator are specified, but raw input traffic data is available only upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel time distributions (quartiles) over the simulation period for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Evaluation scenarios and metrics are clear; reproducibility is limited by non-public raw traffic data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times across 20 independent simulation runs for No Control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Tabulated results follow from the described simulation setup; raw data access is the primary bottleneck.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing mean speed across time and distance for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualization of simulation outcomes is consistent with methodology; raw data is not public.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: On-ramp queue length distributions over time for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Queue length metrics are standard in SUMO; reproducibility depends on non-public input data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios... in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot showing the relationship between signal red ratio and mean queue length.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation logs; parameters for PI-ALINEA and DRL are provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series comparison of mainline occupancy and on-ramp queue length for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly visualizes simulation state variables; limited by raw data availability.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of traffic volume downstream of the merge area at 5-minute intervals.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard traffic flow metric from simulation; raw data is on-request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis of travel time to spatial data removal (perturbation analysis).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation logic is described but specific data masking implementation details are missing.
